Affirm CEO Max Levchin on the 2.5 second limit that has shaped card payments for 60 years, and how Apple and Google Pay worked around it:

"One of the things that's really amazing and subtle about Apple Pay and Google Pay and its interaction with the Visa and Mastercard networks is... Visa and Mastercard have a hard 2.5 second limit on interaction between the network, the issuing bank, and the merchant and the acquiring bank."

"And so the whole thing has to happen in 2.5 seconds, or the transaction gets retried or maybe just cancelled out, and really leaves very little room for any kind of clever innovation."

"Online you can play games. If you're doing e-commerce, you're like, well yes, we're gonna submit your card to Visa, but first we're gonna run some anti-fraud checks, and we're gonna do some other things to reduce liability. But offline, once your card is presented, 2.5 seconds, that's all you got."

"Google and Apple Pay have singularly time-shifted the whole thing by creating secure enclaves inside their chips and saying, 'I already know your card, I can do all kinds of things before I actually have to talk to Visa and Mastercard.'"

"And maybe the shocking thing is that Visa and Mastercard have not yet introduced some new standard saying, actually, it doesn't have to be 2.5 seconds at all. It could be 15 seconds while we go and get a bunch of issuers to bid on better credit quality terms for you, or any other type of innovation."

"But the sort of hard written rules of the Dee Hock era are more or less intact, and that's not 30 years, that's like more, you know, 60 years. And so I think that's probably a critical or more criticizing take on what happened."

So you're up a lot on RH over the last couple of weeks, what do you do about all that juicy profit?

Want to cover this off as efficiently as I can.

1. Always take profit if you're in a financial position where that profit changes your life or pays off debt.

2. Social trading is a net negative for taking profit. On FOMO for example your beautiful uptrending Portfolio value chart will nosedive when you take profit. This is an important point to make as it can impair the ability many will have to take profit in order to avoid that. But again, it needs to be done and who cares, lose the ego, take the money.

3. Also don't take profit. We're in potentially the very early days of a market that will surprise you with how dumb things get. While taking profit on things may feel good, doing so at the early parts of bull markets will leave you chasing and inevitably losing money as you fight to find new coins or rejoin trends. Instead trim positions slowly and utilise the new capital to chase other markets.

Take profit if you need it. 

Fuck what your personal charts look like on social trading platforms.

Hold on to positions that you don't want to chase in the future.

Trim profit instead of full closing.

tweets.text:
Chinese AI labs are forcing the market to compete on the cost of useful intelligence.

Export controls restricted Chinese labs’ access to advanced NVIDIA chips. Staying competitive meant extracting more performance from the hardware available.

In training, Deepseek kept GPUs working while data moved between them and shifted to lower-precision formats that halve memory and compute.

The bigger savings came in serving: sparse models activate only a fraction of their parameters per token, and redesigned attention cut the memory cost of long contexts. The result is models that are cheaper to build and far cheaper to run.

Chinese open-weight models went from under 1.2% of weekly token consumption on OpenRouter in late 2024 to a majority in 2026. 

OpenRouter is a small percentage of global token volumes and its users are price-elastic so this should not be read as global market share. It does show that users will choose cheaper models when switching is easy and performance is good enough.

Cheaper inference also has strategic value for China. These models can already run on domestic accelerators and reduce the country’s dependence on foreign hardware for inference. China still relies largely on foreign chips for frontier training.

China will not have full compute independence until its labs can train frontier models at scale on domestic infrastructure.

#uranium $M.CN $MYRUF

MYRIAD IS DRILLING INTO A HISTORICAL 655 MILLION POUND URANIUM ENDOWMENT

That is the scale of the opportunity at Copper Mountain, and Myriad Uranium is now generating the modern data needed to determine how much of it can ultimately be converted into a compliant resource.

A detailed 1982 study by Bendix Engineering for the U.S. Department of Energy estimated a potential uranium endowment of:

⚛️ Approximately 245 Mlbs eU₃O₈ within the core Control Area
⚛️ Approximately 655 Mlbs eU₃O₈ across the broader Assessment Area
Both estimates extended only to a depth of 600 feet.

These figures are historical and conceptual, not current mineral resources, but they were based on extensive technical work and access to Union Pacific’s enormous dataset. Around 2,000 boreholes were drilled historically at Copper Mountain, with Union Pacific investing an estimated C$125 million in today’s money.

Phase II drilling is now advancing quickly:

🔹 Lucky Cliff: initial results released and assays pending
🔹 Gem: drilling completed and results ahead
🔹 Hesitation: drill team now on site

At Lucky Cliff, all four holes encountered multiple intervals of near-surface uranium mineralization. Myriad reported 50 intervals above 100 ppm eU₃O₈, including 19.96 metres at 269 ppm from only 18 metres and a peak grade of 1,336 ppm.
Crucially, Lucky Cliff lies outside the entire Bendix Assessment Area.
In other words, Myriad has found broad mineralization beyond even the area associated with the historical 655 Mlb endowment estimate.

Drilling has also been completed at Gem, historically estimated to contain 1.44 Mlbs at approximately 0.023% eU₃O₈.

The drill team has now moved to Hesitation, which carries a historical estimate of 2.20 Mlbs at approximately 0.025%.

The investment case is therefore much larger than the initial historical estimate of 26.63 Mlbs.

Myriad is testing a district where historical work suggested hundreds of millions of pounds, and its first Phase II target has already confirmed mineralization beyond the boundaries of that historical assessment.

If modern drilling continues to validate the old geological model, Copper Mountain could emerge as one of the largest undeveloped uranium systems in the United States.

The potential scale is already documented.

Now Myriad is drilling to prove it.

Even solana:J3NKxxXZcnNiMjKw9hYb2K4LUxgwB6t1FtPtQVsv3KFr is actively managed. “Buy and hold forever” is a myth.

Over the past decade, 200+ companies have been removed from the S&P 500 Index and a similar number added. A 2023 study found ~180 stocks have been replaced since 2015 - about one-third of the index. Of the 2010 roster, ~185 tickers were gone by 2026. 

The index is a "living" basket. It promotes what is working and demotes what has broken. That is active management with a committee and a rulebook.

The same lesson applies to individual “great stocks.” 

$PYPL was a generational compounder until July 2021 at ~$306. It then lost more than 80% of its value. 

$LULU printed $511 at the end of 2023; it is now around $122 (~80% decline). 

$TTD ran to ~$140 in December 2024, then suffered an ~90% drawdown.

$NKE and $BA remained household names and index members while years of gains vanished. 

$ENPH, $WBA, $PAYC and $MTCH were later removed after the damage was already done. 

That is the point most buy-and-hold sermons skip. Quality is not a substitute for timing. Leadership decays. Growth slows. Multiples compress. A stock can be an excellent business and still destroy capital if you own it through a Stage 4 decline. 

The index itself does not “hold forever.” It sells the laggards - often late, but it sells them. 

At AlphaTarget we treat all this with discipline. We combine fundamental research with technical analysis to identify the leading disruptive growth stocks, then use Stage Analysis to time entries and exits: accumulate in emerging Stage 2 uptrends, ride the trend while the tape confirms, and step aside when the structure breaks. 

The aim is not to marry a ticker. It is to own leadership while it is leadership - so we can hold onto the years of gains that disappear in months. The market does not pay you for loyalty - it pays you for being in the right stocks, at the right time. Another reason why semis are hard (and more broadly, equities), and no longer the hot ball of money is because things are no longer linear, easy to understand

Longing most "global trends" generate the most returns - in 2021, you long crypto (it was the biggest thing); 2023, financials, 2025, semis

These homerun trades often focus on one core theme: Demand is increasing, this benefits. And most homerun trades, if you look in the past 5 years, have all come from this simple seed

The moment a thematic starts becoming more complex, it fails. Investors become uncertain if what they're holding is what will be needed. And that's where AI is right now.

Take a look at AVGO's earnings. AVGO reported extraordinary numbers - F3Q revenue +85.5% YoY - and introduced FY27/FY28 AI revenue targets of $115B/$230B. FY28 potentially supports >$30 EPS. 

But AVGO sold off because FY27 was below buyside expectations of ~$130–150B and the growth increasingly depends on OpenAI + Anthropic. Around 15GW of the roughly 20GW FY28 deployment discussed comes from those two customers. 

On the other hand, software, which was thought to be left for dead, is incredibly strong. SNOW is up 16% - Product growth accelerated sharply, about half the acceleration came from AI products, CoCo adoption reached ~63%, cRPO accelerated, and margins are holding up better than expected. 

All of a sudden, software may be the enterprise control plane for AI agents? No one knows. And so the AI trade is basically unwinding on itself, because its so hard to forecast the future

Markets are ever-evolving, and so, IMO, it's more worthwhile to figure out where the puck will be 6 months from now
